title: Dreams
subtitle: A place to make and play
summary: Dreams is Media Molecule's PlayStation 4 creation game, released on 14 February 2020. Players can build games, scenes, music and animated experiences, then share them with others. Browsing a creation and opening its parts belongs to the same environment, making play an introduction to what might be made next. An imp acts as the player's cursor and presence within the tools. The range extends from a small object to a complete playable world, with characters, sound and behaviour assembled inside the same console application.
body: Dreams is Media Molecule's PlayStation 4 creation game, released on 14 February 2020. Players can build games, scenes, music and animated experiences, then share them with others. Browsing a creation and opening its parts belongs to the same environment, making play an introduction to what might be made next. An imp acts as the player's cursor and presence within the tools. The range extends from a small object to a complete playable world, with characters, sound and behaviour assembled inside the same console application.

Objects and creations can be shared for reuse when their makers permit it. A player can take an existing element, change it and combine it with other work, making a larger project possible without constructing every part from nothing. Sculpting and painting give forms their appearance, while logic connects actions and responses. Music tools add another route into the process. The controller can be used through motion or analogue input, and the imp can enter a character so the maker can test the scene from inside it.

Media Molecule supplied tutorials and its own Art's Dream adventure to demonstrate how the tools could work together. Community curation helped guide players through the growing library, where small experiments could appear beside more complete games. That variety made Dreams as much a place to encounter other makers as a set of editing tools. The studio ended live development support in September 2023 while retaining the existing online service. Its history shows the possibilities and practical limits of making a creation platform whose work remains inside one console ecosystem.
